title: Apple Icon Composer
lede: Apple’s 2025 tool for building layered app icons from Liquid Glass, with controls for specular light, blur, translucency, and shadow.
summary: Apple’s icon tool, which exposes the glass material as sliders. 2025.

evidence.note: Inspected the Apple Newsroom image Apple-WWDC25-Liquid-Glass-Icon-Composer-250609 (1960 × 1102, large_2x variant) in a scratchpad copy. A press render. Not stored.

styles.note: Names the parts of the material in its own interface: specular, blur, translucency, dark, and shadow, applied to stacked layers.

context: Apple: Icon Composer annotates “layers for multiple rendering modes, with advanced features that include blurring, adjusting translucency, testing specular highlights, and previewing icons in various tints”. [Apple Newsroom](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/06/apple-supercharges-its-tools-and-technologies-for-developers/).

Apple: “the Dock, app icons, and widgets have all been crafted from multiple layers of Liquid Glass … with specular highlights”. [Apple Newsroom](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/06/apple-introduces-a-delightful-and-elegant-new-software-design/).
observed: A Mac window with three parts over a blue wave wallpaper: a layer list on the left, a large preview of the Podcasts icon in the middle, and an inspector on the right.
The icon is built from stacked translucent layers: a blue rounded square, two pale rings, and a white figure. Each layer has a lit rim, and the rings show the blue square through them.
The inspector has a “Liquid Glass” group with Mode (Individual), Specular (on), Blur 21.8 %, Translucency 50 %, Dark 42 %, and Shadow (Neutral, 50 %).
The toolbar is a row of separate capsules: appearance toggle, grid, light angle (34°), and zoom (50 %). Small previews at the bottom show the icon in default, dark, and mono looks.
The sidebar and inspector are light, translucent panels inset in the window with rounded corners.
interpretation: The tool turns the material into a short list of parameters with a single light direction. This is close to how a CSS version must work: a fill, a blur, a highlight angle, and a shadow.
borrow: Fix one light angle for the whole interface, and place every specular highlight on the edge that faces it.

rights.statement: Apple press image of copyrighted software and icons. No image is stored here.
